detail.longDescription: I run Glama – MCP server registry. For 2 years now, we have been indexing and tracking every open-source server. More recently, there has been an uptick in emails from users claiming to be EU residents, and demanding the removal of their projects from the website because it contains their contact details (username, avatar, or contact detail mentions in the source code). Historically, the approach we took that if someone requests to remove their source code, and source code does not include valid license, we would remove it. However, if the source code was released under GNU, MIT or similarly permissive license, we would reject the request. What's the correct way to handle these requests in the context of open-source and properly licensed codebase that includes people contact details (or identifiers such as usernames, avatars, etc)?
